You are the cold reviewer screening a process definition, round 3 (fresh context; you have seen nothing before). Read only the two files named here — nothing else.

- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/process-definition.fitness.md
- artifact: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/typedef-rendering.md

Prompt: "State, as judge_stamp, the model and prompt version you judge as. Read the criteria set at criteria_path and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact against every scenario. Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name, the quoted text, the change, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the PM role decides from the review alone. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes."

Return exactly this structure:
judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v6
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, or "uncovered">
  section: <section of the artifact>
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the criteria. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file. Judge all of it, including the steps YAML and every loop's exit.

# Fitness set: process-definition

These scenarios are evaluated by the `cold-reviewer` role, never
executed; the compiler and linter carry the mechanical half of the
same requirements. The mapping table compiles each Then into the
judge-rubric assertion the reviewer scores. The scenarios project the
[process-definition typedef](../artifacts/process-definition.md)'s
requirements and the
[process-definition guideline](../guidelines/process-definition.md)'s
rules into a judge's rubric.

## Scenarios

Scenario 1: the definition is the single source its renderings claim
  Given the process definition, its flow diagram, and its rendered
  skill
  When the diagram and skill are compared to the steps section
  Then both correspond to the steps exactly — every step, prompt, and
  branch present, nothing added — and both declare themselves
  generated, never hand-edited

Scenario 2: every outcome has a live witness
  Given the outcomes list and the steps section
  When each outcome's named witness is looked up
  Then every outcome names a step, check, or branch that exists, and a
  reader can say from the witness alone whether the outcome held for a
  run

Scenario 3: every loop declares its exits
  Given every cycle in the flow
  When its branch rows are read
  Then each cycle carries a labeled reached-state success exit, a
  round or budget cap, or both — no loop can run unbounded

Scenario 4: steps read only what they list
  Given each step's prompt, checks, and run template
  When every reference in them is resolved
  Then each resolves to a declared input or output of that step, and
  no prompt directs the agent to load undeclared context

Scenario 5: the run returns the artifact
  Given the result declaration and the purpose
  When they are compared
  Then the run returns the artifact it exists to produce, or result is
  absent and the outcomes pin the run's value

Scenario 6: prose sits where prose belongs
  Given every step record and the guiding statement
  When each is read
  Then step prose appears only in prompt fields, and the guiding
  statement (when present) states a cross-step judgment, never a
  sequence

## Compile mapping (each Then/And → one judge-rubric assertion)

| Scenario Then | Judge-rubric assertion |
|---|---|
| 1 — renderings correspond | "Walk the diagram and skill against the steps: name any step, prompt, or branch missing or added, and any rendering not marked generated. Empty list = pass." |
| 2 — outcomes witnessed | "For each outcome, name the witnessing step/check/branch and confirm it exists. Any outcome with a missing or unverifiable witness = fail, cite it." |
| 3 — loop exits declared | "List every cycle and its labeled exits. Any cycle without a success exit or cap = fail, cite it." |
| 4 — declared reads only | "For each step, quote any reference in prompt/checks/run that is not a declared input or output, and any prompt directing undeclared context loads. Empty list = pass." |
| 5 — artifact result | "Name the result value and what the purpose says the run produces. Mismatch, or a status-shaped result = fail; absent result justified by value-pinning outcomes = pass." |
| 6 — prose placement | "Quote any prose in a step outside prompt, and quote the guiding statement if it sequences steps. Empty list = pass." |

## Sources

G-Eval–style rubric decomposition for the mapping table; the tests
project the process-definition typedef's checklist and Commitment and
the guideline's rules, per the definition-chain shape the

1 --- 2 type: process-definition 3 id: typedef-rendering-process 4 owner: product-authority 5 status: draft 6 version: 3 7 created: 2026-09-05 8 updated: 2026-09-05 9 produces: [] 10 carried-by: typedef-rendering-skill 11 condition-language: cel 12 annotations: 13 claude-code: 14 activation: model-judged 15 promotion: experiment-local 16 use-when: "an approved typedef carrying its writing rules and fitness scenarios changes or lands, a guideline or fitness set at its load point stands in doubt — missing, not current with its typedef, written by hand, or left by a typedef that no longer qualifies — or the shop must confirm that every such typedef has both of its texts current" 17 --- 18 19 # Process: Typedef rendering 20 21 **Purpose:** Keep the two texts of every artifact type current with 22 the type's one standard. An *artifact type* is a kind of document the 23 shop produces; its *typedef* is the single source the type is 24 generated from, a definition under `basis/artifacts/`. A typedef that 25 stands approved and carries a "Writing rules" section and a "Fitness 26 scenarios" section is the type's standard, and this process calls such 27 a typedef *qualifying*. Its two texts are *renderings* — generated 28 outputs, never edited by hand, never the source: the *guideline*, the 29 maker's text, the type's writing rules read by whoever makes an 30 artifact of the type; and the *fitness set*, the checker's text, the 31 judged Given/When/Then scenarios a check screens an artifact against. 32 Each stands at a *load point*, the directory its readers read it from: 33 `basis/guidelines/` for guidelines and `basis/fitness/` for fitness 34 sets. The process checks what stands at the two load points against a 35 fresh render of each qualifying typedef by the *compiler* — the tool 36 of the *lead shop*, this repository, the shop that owns the product's 37 definitions — that produces both texts from a typedef, and reconciles 38 every difference through the compiler — so that a maker and a checker 39 of the type work from the same words, a change to the typedef reaches 40 both texts, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that they do. 41 42 **Guiding statement:** A rendering is never the source of truth. 43 Whatever stands at a qualifying typedef's output path, or names a 44 typedef not in `approved` as its source, that a fresh render would not 45 put there is a finding, and every finding resolves toward the typedef 46 — a re-render by the compiler, a removal, or the owner's decision on 47 the typedef — never an edit to a rendered text, and never an edit to 48 the typedef made to match one. 49 50 **Outcomes:** the definition of good for this process is the feature 51 [feat-typedef-rendering](../../features/feat-typedef-rendering.md); 52 each outcome names the scenarios of that feature it witnesses. 53 - O1. Every qualifying typedef has both of its texts at their load 54 points, each byte-equal to a fresh render of that typedef, and the 55 check reports no finding of any kind — witnessed by `route`'s first 56 success exit, on empty `open` with empty `escalations` (feature 57 scenarios 3 and 5: after a run, each text is current with its 58 typedef as it now stands). 59 - O2. The texts land where the checks already read, and nowhere else: 60 a type's guideline at `/.md` and its fitness set 61 at `/.fitness.md`, `` the type key the 62 typedef's `defines` names — the paths read today by the checks that 63 screen an artifact against its type's texts and by the *linter*, 64 `basis/tools/lint_basis.py`, the check the tree runs on every 65 definition — and no step of this process writes to or edits a 66 check's definition — witnessed by `reconcile`'s render into those 67 two paths, by `check`'s diff and sweep over those two directories 68 and no other, and by the O2 row of the Derived checks table below 69 (feature scenario 6). 70 - O3. A typedef that does not qualify yields no text a maker or a 71 check reads: `enumerate` admits only qualifying typedefs and its list 72 is the set `check` renders against, and a `stale` rendering (O4) is 73 removed at reconciliation — witnessed by `enumerate`'s run, its 74 `approved` read by `check`, and the stale rows of `open` consumed by 75 `reconcile` (the feature's constraint C6: a text produced from a typedef not yet approved is read by no maker 76 and no check). 77 - O4. The check reports every defect as a row of one of five kinds, 78 named here and nowhere else. The row's first word is the kind and 79 its second word its subject; for `missing`, `diverged`, 80 `hand-written`, and `stale` the third word is the path the 81 reconciliation acts on, and `will-not-compile` acts on its subject 82 and carries the reason as the remainder. Three kinds are the 83 compiler's rows, one run per typedef in `approved`: `missing 84 ` — a text absent from its load point; `diverged 85 ` — a text not byte-equal to a fresh render of its typedef, 86 whatever the cause, a hand edit or a typedef amended after its 87 render — where `` is the produced text's id, `-guideline` 88 or `-fitness`, so the row names the text, and `` is 89 the typedef's path, added by `check` as the third word, so the row 90 names the type; `will-not-compile ` — a typedef in 91 `approved` the compiler does not render, its subject the typedef's 92 path as the compiler prints it, and for which the compiler writes 93 no `missing` or `diverged` row, so an unrenderable typedef never 94 also burns the run toward the cap — one `will-not-compile` row is 95 `check`'s own, not the compiler's: a typedef in `approved` with no 96 `defines` key, reason "no defines key", written before the compiler 97 is called. Two kinds are `check`'s own 98 sweep of the load points: `stale ` — a rendering 99 whose `source` key names a typedef not in `approved`; `hand-written 100 ` — a file at a qualifying typedef's output path 101 that carries no `generated` key; the subject of a sweep row is a 102 path — witnessed by the rows of `findings` that `check` writes 103 (feature scenario 4). 104 - O5. Every finding reaches its consumer and resolves toward the 105 typedef: `missing`, `diverged`, and `hand-written` are re-rendered by 106 the compiler, which produces the type's two texts together, so both 107 are current with the typedef as it now stands after reconciliation; 108 `stale` is removed; `will-not-compile` lands as a review entry in 109 that typedef's Document History. An escalation never ends with the 110 run and never burns it: a row whose subject is already named in 111 `escalations` is not open, so a check clean of open rows with 112 escalations standing routes through `report`, which files each row 113 into the governed record the owner reads — witnessed by `filter`'s 114 run, `reconcile`'s prompt, `route`'s clean-with-escalations branch, 115 and `report`'s prompt (feature scenarios 3 and 5). 116 117 **Roles:** reconciler and reporter — 118 [`../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md`](../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md) 119 (the compilers and the lint are this role's apparatus; it consumes the 120 check's findings, and its resulting action per finding is a re-render, 121 a removal, or an escalation). The owner — the product authority, who 122 owns and approves every typedef — decides every escalated typedef 123 change; that decision lands through the typedef's own history, not 124 through a step of this process. The check itself is mechanical and 125 runs by the runtime against the qualifying typedefs and the compiler's 126 rendering contract, so the definition of good sits outside the role 127 that reconciles. 128 129 **Carried by:** `.claude/skills/typedef-rendering/SKILL.md` — generated 130 from this definition by 131 [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never 132 edited by hand, and placed at the skills load point by the 133 [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) process once this definition 134 stands approved. Until that run the carrier does not exist, so its 135 correspondence to this definition cannot be walked at screening time: 136 skill-rendering's own check — a fresh render diffed against what 137 stands — is the check of that correspondence, as it is for every 138 approved process. 139 140 ## Flow (compiled) 141 142 Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not 143 edit by hand. 144 145 ```mermaid 146 flowchart TD 147 enumerate["Enumerate the qualifying typedefs — runtime
in — definitions: string
out — approved: string[]"] 148 check["Check the load points against a fresh render — runtime
in — approved: string[], compiler: string, guidelines: string, fitness: string
out — findings: string[]"] 149 filter["Filter the findings to the rows still open — runtime
in — findings: string[], escalations: string[]
out — open: string[]"] 150 route{"Route on the open rows
in — open: string[], escalations: string[], round: integer, round_cap: integer"} 151 reconcile(["Reconcile the open rows — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], guidelines: string, fitness: string, compiler: string, escalations: string[]
out — escalations: string[]"]) 152 advance_round["Advance the round — runtime
in — round: integer
sets — round: integer"] 153 report(["Report the rows left open — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], escalations: string[], self: string
out — escalations: string[]"]) 154 __end(("end")) 155 __start(("start")) --> enumerate 156 enumerate --> check 157 check --> filter 158 filter --> route 159 route -->|success exit: check clean, nothing escalated — every qualifying typedef's two texts current| __end 160 route -->|success exit: no row open — escalations filed through report| report 161 route -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with rows open| report 162 route -->|else| reconcile 163 reconcile --> advance_round 164 advance_round --> check 165 report --> __end 166 ``` 167 168 169 ## Data 170 171 Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema 172 names inline; conditions are CEL expressions over these names. Paths 173 are relative to the lead shop's repository root, the run's working 174 directory. The design decision the process rests on is 175 [adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../../decisions/adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md). 176 177 **Qualification.** `definitions` names the directory of the lead 178 shop's typedefs and nothing else. A typedef *qualifies* when its 179 front-matter carries `status: approved` and its body carries the 180 second-level headings `## Writing rules` and `## Fitness scenarios` — 181 the two sections the 182 [artifact-typedef typedef](../artifacts/artifact-typedef.md), the 183 definition of what a typedef is, requires of a type whose texts are 184 produced (its required sections 6, Writing rules, and 7, Fitness 185 scenarios), and the sections the compiler reads. `enumerate` tests 186 exactly that, and `approved` is the one enumeration of what qualifies: 187 `check` runs the compiler over that list and no other, so no second 188 reading of "qualifying" can disagree with `enumerate`. 189 190 **Paths.** `guidelines` and `fitness` are the two load points. A 191 type's texts stand there as `/.md` and 192 `/.fitness.md`, `` the value of the typedef's 193 `defines` key — the compiler's own naming, read the same way by 194 `check`'s diff, `check`'s sweep, and `reconcile`'s re-render, so all 195 three act on the same paths. A qualifying typedef with no `defines` 196 key has no output path to name, so `check` writes the 197 `will-not-compile` row for it itself (O4) and neither calls the 198 compiler nor sweeps for it. `self` is this definition, the governed 199 record a path-only escalation lands in. 200 201 **Compiler contract.** `compiler` is the tool. Run as `python3 202 --guideline --fitness ` it produces 203 the type's two texts together, each with front-matter that carries 204 `generated`, `source` — the typedef's path as `approved` lists it — 205 and `source-digest`. Run with `--check` and the same two path options 206 it renders to scratch and diffs against what stands at those paths, 207 printing its rows or nothing, and never writes a load point — the load 208 points are written only at reconciliation's re-render, where that 209 write is the point. In every row it prints the typedef's path as given 210 on its command line, which is the path `approved` lists. Its check 211 exits zero with its `missing` and `diverged` rows or with none, exits 212 one with a `will-not-compile` row, and exits two with no row on a 213 usage error. The one `will-not-compile` row the compiler does not 214 write is `check`'s own row for a typedef with no `defines` key, in 215 the compiler's row shape. 216 217 **Rows and escalations.** `findings` holds every row the check 218 writes, one per line, in the five kinds O4 names. A `string[]` value 219 interpolates newline-joined into a `run` script — one row per line, 220 so rows may carry spaces and word-splitting is never the contract for 221 a row list; `filter.run` and `check.run` quote each interpolation of 222 a row list for that reason, while `for def in ${approved}` stands 223 unquoted because there the split into paths is the intent and the 224 paths carry no spaces. `open` holds the rows still to act on — a row 225 is open until its subject, the row's second word, is the first word 226 of a row of `escalations`, matched whole, so a row already filed to 227 the owner recurs in `findings` every round without recurring in 228 `open`. Every row of `escalations` therefore begins with the subject 229 it settles — a produced text's id, a typedef's path, or a path at a 230 load point — followed by what was filed. The run entry `report` 231 writes into `self` changes the source of this process's carrier, so 232 skill-rendering's next check reports the carrier `diverged` and 233 re-renders it — the dynamic the shop records as lead-ghaiq; the run 234 entry stays in `self`, as the sibling processes make it. A write to a typedef whose 235 path is listed in `approved` — the review entry `reconcile` or 236 `report` puts in its Document History — is a write to a declared 237 input, as the `reconcile` and `report` steps of 238 [role-rendering](role-rendering.md) make; no output is declared for 239 it. 240 241 **Failure semantics.** A `run` step that exits nonzero is a failed 242 step, not an empty result: the run halts at that step and the failure 243 is reported to the reconciler role — it is never read as empty 244 `findings` and never routed as a clean check. The compiler's rows, 245 not its exit status, are its verdict, so `check.run` treats a 246 compiler exit that is nonzero with no row printed as the failed step 247 — the compiler could not check — and a nonzero exit with rows printed 248 as the rows. 249 250 **What is not a finding.** Two kinds the sibling rendering processes 251 — [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) and 252 [role-rendering](role-rendering.md) — report do not apply here and 253 are not written. `unrecognized`: a file at a load point that names no 254 `source` and stands at no qualifying typedef's output path is outside 255 this process — the base writing style, the six experience guidelines, 256 and the interaction fitness set have no artifact type behind them, 257 and their source is a question the design decision lists as not 258 decided. `second-home`: each text has one load point, so no second 259 rendering home exists. Also not a finding: a file at a load point 260 whose `source` names a typedef in `approved` but which stands at a 261 path other than that typedef's output path — the compiler reports 262 `missing` at the right path and the re-render fills it; the stray 263 file is the owner's sweep, filed as a follow-on question in this 264 definition's Document History. During the transition, a hand-written 265 file at a qualifying typedef's output path yields both a 266 `hand-written` row from the sweep and, since it is not byte-equal to 267 a fresh render, a `diverged` row from the compiler; one re-render 268 clears both. The run declares no `result`: `produces` is empty 269 because the run's value is state change — every qualifying typedef's 270 two texts current at their load points — and O1's witness pins it. 271 272 ```yaml 273 data: 274 definitions: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/artifacts} 275 compiler: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/tools/compile_typedef.py} 276 guidelines: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/guidelines} 277 fitness: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/fitness} 278 self: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/processes/typedef-rendering.md} 279 approved: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 280 findings: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 281 open: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 282 escalations: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 283 round: {type: integer, initial: 1} 284 round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3} 285 ``` 286 287 ## Steps 288 289 ```yaml 290 start: enumerate 291 steps: 292 - id: enumerate 293 name: Enumerate the qualifying typedefs 294 run-by: {execution: runtime} 295 inputs: [definitions] 296 outputs: [approved] 297 run: | 298 for def in ${definitions}/*.md; do 299 awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit 1} NR > 1 && !body && /^---$/ {body = 1; next} !body && /^status: approved$/ {a = 1} body && /^## Writing rules$/ {w = 1} body && /^## Fitness scenarios$/ {s = 1} END {exit !(a && w && s)}' "$def" \ 300 && printf '%s\n' "$def" 301 done | sort 302 next: check 303 304 - id: check 305 name: Check the load points against a fresh render 306 run-by: {execution: runtime} 307 inputs: [approved, compiler, guidelines, fitness] 308 outputs: [findings] 309 run: | 310 for def in ${approved}; do 311 type=$(awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && sub(/^defines: */, "") {print; exit}' "$def") 312 [ -n "$type" ] || { printf 'will-not-compile %s no defines key\n' "$def"; continue; } 313 rows=$(python3 ${compiler} "$def" --check --guideline ${guidelines}/$type.md --fitness ${fitness}/$type.fitness.md) \ 314 || { rc=$?; [ -n "$rows" ] || exit $rc; } 315 [ -z "$rows" ] || printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -v def="$def" '$1 == "missing" || $1 == "diverged" { $2 = $2 " " def } { print }' 316 for file in ${guidelines}/$type.md ${fitness}/$type.fitness.md; --- type: process-definition id: typedef-rendering-process owner: product-authority status: draft version: 3 created: 2026-09-05 updated: 2026-09-05 produces: [] carried-by: typedef-rendering-skill condition-language: cel annotations: claude-code: activation: model-judged promotion: experiment-local use-when: "an approved typedef carrying its writing rules and fitness scenarios changes or lands, a guideline or fitness set at its load point stands in doubt — missing, not current with its typedef, written by hand, or left by a typedef that no longer qualifies — or the shop must confirm that every such typedef has both of its texts current" --- # Process: Typedef rendering **Purpose:** Keep the two texts of every artifact type current with the type's one standard. An *artifact type* is a kind of document the shop produces; its *typedef* is the single source the type is generated from, a definition under `basis/artifacts/`. A typedef that stands approved and carries a "Writing rules" section and a "Fitness scenarios" section is the type's standard, and this process calls such a typedef *qualifying*. Its two texts are *renderings* — generated outputs, never edited by hand, never the source: the *guideline*, the maker's text, the type's writing rules read by whoever makes an artifact of the type; and the *fitness set*, the checker's text, the judged Given/When/Then scenarios a check screens an artifact against. Each stands at a *load point*, the directory its readers read it from: `basis/guidelines/` for guidelines and `basis/fitness/` for fitness sets. The process checks what stands at the two load points against a fresh render of each qualifying typedef by the *compiler* — the tool of the *lead shop*, this repository, the shop that owns the product's definitions — that produces both texts from a typedef, and reconciles every difference through the compiler — so that a maker and a checker of the type work from the same words, a change to the typedef reaches both texts, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that they do. **Guiding statement:** A rendering is never the source of truth. Whatever stands at a qualifying typedef's output path, or names a typedef not in `approved` as its source, that a fresh render would not put there is a finding, and every finding resolves toward the typedef — a re-render by the compiler, a removal, or the owner's decision on the typedef — never an edit to a rendered text, and never an edit to the typedef made to match one. **Outcomes:** the definition of good for this process is the feature [feat-typedef-rendering](../../features/feat-typedef-rendering.md); each outcome names the scenarios of that feature it witnesses. - O1. Every qualifying typedef has both of its texts at their load points, each byte-equal to a fresh render of that typedef, and the check reports no finding of any kind — witnessed by `route`'s first success exit, on empty `open` with empty `escalations` (feature scenarios 3 and 5: after a run, each text is current with its typedef as it now stands). - O2. The texts land where the checks already read, and nowhere else: a type's guideline at `/.md` and its fitness set at `/.fitness.md`, `` the type key the typedef's `defines` names — the paths read today by the checks that screen an artifact against its type's texts and by the *linter*, `basis/tools/lint_basis.py`, the check the tree runs on every definition — and no step of this process writes to or edits a check's definition — witnessed by `reconcile`'s render into those two paths, by `check`'s diff and sweep over those two directories and no other, and by the O2 row of the Derived checks table below (feature scenario 6). - O3. A typedef that does not qualify yields no text a maker or a check reads: `enumerate` admits only qualifying typedefs and its list is the set `check` renders against, and a `stale` rendering (O4) is removed at reconciliation — witnessed by `enumerate`'s run, its `approved` read by `check`, and the stale rows of `open` consumed by `reconcile` (the feature's constraint C6: a text produced from a typedef not yet approved is read by no maker and no check). - O4. The check reports every defect as a row of one of five kinds, named here and nowhere else. The row's first word is the kind and its second word its subject; for `missing`, `diverged`, `hand-written`, and `stale` the third word is the path the reconciliation acts on, and `will-not-compile` acts on its subject and carries the reason as the remainder. Three kinds are the compiler's rows, one run per typedef in `approved`: `missing ` — a text absent from its load point; `diverged ` — a text not byte-equal to a fresh render of its typedef, whatever the cause, a hand edit or a typedef amended after its render — where `` is the produced text's id, `-guideline` or `-fitness`, so the row names the text, and `` is the typedef's path, added by `check` as the third word, so the row names the type; `will-not-compile ` — a typedef in `approved` the compiler does not render, its subject the typedef's path as the compiler prints it, and for which the compiler writes no `missing` or `diverged` row, so an unrenderable typedef never also burns the run toward the cap — one `will-not-compile` row is `check`'s own, not the compiler's: a typedef in `approved` with no `defines` key, reason "no defines key", written before the compiler is called. Two kinds are `check`'s own sweep of the load points: `stale ` — a rendering whose `source` key names a typedef not in `approved`; `hand-written ` — a file at a qualifying typedef's output path that carries no `generated` key; the subject of a sweep row is a path — witnessed by the rows of `findings` that `check` writes (feature scenario 4). - O5. Every finding reaches its consumer and resolves toward the typedef: `missing`, `diverged`, and `hand-written` are re-rendered by the compiler, which produces the type's two texts together, so both are current with the typedef as it now stands after reconciliation; `stale` is removed; `will-not-compile` lands as a review entry in that typedef's Document History. An escalation never ends with the run and never burns it: a row whose subject is already named in `escalations` is not open, so a check clean of open rows with escalations standing routes through `report`, which files each row into the governed record the owner reads — witnessed by `filter`'s run, `reconcile`'s prompt, `route`'s clean-with-escalations branch, and `report`'s prompt (feature scenarios 3 and 5). **Roles:** reconciler and reporter — [`../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md`](../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md) (the compilers and the lint are this role's apparatus; it consumes the check's findings, and its resulting action per finding is a re-render, a removal, or an escalation). The owner — the product authority, who owns and approves every typedef — decides every escalated typedef change; that decision lands through the typedef's own history, not through a step of this process. The check itself is mechanical and runs by the runtime against the qualifying typedefs and the compiler's rendering contract, so the definition of good sits outside the role that reconciles. **Carried by:** `.claude/skills/typedef-rendering/SKILL.md` — generated from this definition by [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never edited by hand, and placed at the skills load point by the [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) process once this definition stands approved. Until that run the carrier does not exist, so its correspondence to this definition cannot be walked at screening time: skill-rendering's own check — a fresh render diffed against what stands — is the check of that correspondence, as it is for every approved process. ## Flow (compiled) Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not edit by hand. ```mermaid flowchart TD enumerate["Enumerate the qualifying typedefs — runtime
in — definitions: string
out — approved: string[]"] check["Check the load points against a fresh render — runtime
in — approved: string[], compiler: string, guidelines: string, fitness: string
out — findings: string[]"] filter["Filter the findings to the rows still open — runtime
in — findings: string[], escalations: string[]
out — open: string[]"] route{"Route on the open rows
in — open: string[], escalations: string[], round: integer, round_cap: integer"} reconcile(["Reconcile the open rows — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], guidelines: string, fitness: string, compiler: string, escalations: string[]
out — escalations: string[]"]) advance_round["Advance the round — runtime
in — round: integer
sets — round: integer"] report(["Report the rows left open — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], escalations: string[], self: string
out — escalations: string[]"]) __end(("end")) __start(("start")) --> enumerate enumerate --> check check --> filter filter --> route route -->|success exit: check clean, nothing escalated — every qualifying typedef's two texts current| __end route -->|success exit: no row open — escalations filed through report| report route -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with rows open| report route -->|else| reconcile reconcile --> advance_round advance_round --> check report --> __end ``` ## Data Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema names inline; conditions are CEL expressions over these names. Paths are relative to the lead shop's repository root, the run's working directory. The design decision the process rests on is [adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../../decisions/adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md). **Qualification.** `definitions` names the directory of the lead shop's typedefs and nothing else. A typedef *qualifies* when its front-matter carries `status: approved` and its body carries the second-level headings `## Writing rules` and `## Fitness scenarios` — the two sections the [artifact-typedef typedef](../artifacts/artifact-typedef.md), the definition of what a typedef is, requires of a type whose texts are produced (its required sections 6, Writing rules, and 7, Fitness scenarios), and the sections the compiler reads. `enumerate` tests exactly that, and `approved` is the one enumeration of what qualifies: `check` runs the compiler over that list and no other, so no second reading of "qualifying" can disagree with `enumerate`. **Paths.** `guidelines` and `fitness` are the two load points. A type's texts stand there as `/.md` and `/.fitness.md`, `` the value of the typedef's `defines` key — the compiler's own naming, read the same way by `check`'s diff, `check`'s sweep, and `reconcile`'s re-render, so all three act on the same paths. A qualifying typedef with no `defines` key has no output path to name, so `check` writes the `will-not-compile` row for it itself (O4) and neither calls the compiler nor sweeps for it. `self` is this definition, the governed record a path-only escalation lands in. **Compiler contract.** `compiler` is the tool. Run as `python3 --guideline --fitness ` it produces the type's two texts together, each with front-matter that carries `generated`, `source` — the typedef's path as `approved` lists it — and `source-digest`. Run with `--check` and the same two path options it renders to scratch and diffs against what stands at those paths, printing its rows or nothing, and never writes a load point — the load points are written only at reconciliation's re-render, where that write is the point. In every row it prints the typedef's path as given on its command line, which is the path `approved` lists. Its check exits zero with its `missing` and `diverged` rows or with none, exits one with a `will-not-compile` row, and exits two with no row on a usage error. The one `will-not-compile` row the compiler does not write is `check`'s own row for a typedef with no `defines` key, in the compiler's row shape. **Rows and escalations.** `findings` holds every row the check writes, one per line, in the five kinds O4 names. A `string[]` value interpolates newline-joined into a `run` script — one row per line, so rows may carry spaces and word-splitting is never the contract for a row list; `filter.run` and `check.run` quote each interpolation of a row list for that reason, while `for def in ${approved}` stands unquoted because there the split into paths is the intent and the paths carry no spaces. `open` holds the rows still to act on — a row is open until its subject, the row's second word, is the first word of a row of `escalations`, matched whole, so a row already filed to the owner recurs in `findings` every round without recurring in `open`. Every row of `escalations` therefore begins with the subject it settles — a produced text's id, a typedef's path, or a path at a load point — followed by what was filed. The run entry `report` writes into `self` changes the source of this process's carrier, so skill-rendering's next check reports the carrier `diverged` and re-renders it — the dynamic the shop records as lead-ghaiq; the run entry stays in `self`, as the sibling processes make it. A write to a typedef whose path is listed in `approved` — the review entry `reconcile` or `report` puts in its Document History — is a write to a declared input, as the `reconcile` and `report` steps of [role-rendering](role-rendering.md) make; no output is declared for it. **Failure semantics.** A `run` step that exits nonzero is a failed step, not an empty result: the run halts at that step and the failure is reported to the reconciler role — it is never read as empty `findings` and never routed as a clean check. The compiler's rows, not its exit status, are its verdict, so `check.run` treats a compiler exit that is nonzero with no row printed as the failed step — the compiler could not check — and a nonzero exit with rows printed as the rows. **What is not a finding.** Two kinds the sibling rendering processes — [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) and [role-rendering](role-rendering.md) — report do not apply here and are not written. `unrecognized`: a file at a load point that names no `source` and stands at no qualifying typedef's output path is outside this process — the base writing style, the six experience guidelines, and the interaction fitness set have no artifact type behind them, and their source is a question the design decision lists as not decided. `second-home`: each text has one load point, so no second rendering home exists. Also not a finding: a file at a load point whose `source` names a typedef in `approved` but which stands at a path other than that typedef's output path — the compiler reports `missing` at the right path and the re-render fills it; the stray file is the owner's sweep, filed as a follow-on question in this definition's Document History. During the transition, a hand-written file at a qualifying typedef's output path yields both a `hand-written` row from the sweep and, since it is not byte-equal to a fresh render, a `diverged` row from the compiler; one re-render clears both. The run declares no `result`: `produces` is empty because the run's value is state change — every qualifying typedef's two texts current at their load points — and O1's witness pins it. ```yaml data: definitions: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/artifacts} compiler: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/tools/compile_typedef.py} guidelines: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/guidelines} fitness: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/fitness} self: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/processes/typedef-rendering.md} approved: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} findings: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} open: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} escalations: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} round: {type: integer, initial: 1} round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3} ``` ## Steps ```yaml start: enumerate steps: - id: enumerate name: Enumerate the qualifying typedefs run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [definitions] outputs: [approved] run: | for def in ${definitions}/*.md; do [ -n "$row" ] || continue subject=$(printf '%s\n' "$row" | cut -d' ' -f2) printf '%s\n' "${escalations}" | cut -d' ' -f1 | grep -qxF -- "$subject" \ || printf '%s\n' "$row" done next: route - id: route name: Route on the open rows run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [open, escalations, round, round_cap] branches: - label: "success exit: check clean, nothing escalated — every qualifying typedef's two texts current" when: size(open) == 0 && size(escalations) == 0 next: end - label: "success exit: no row open — escalations filed through report" when: size(open) == 0 next: report - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with rows open" when: round >= round_cap next: report - else: reconcile - id: reconcile name: Reconcile the open rows run-by: {role: lead-solutions-architect, execution: agent} inputs: [open, approved, guidelines, fitness, compiler, escalations] outputs: [escalations] prompt: | Act on each row of open by its kind, the first word;
